Our contributions are summarized as follows:
• This paper proposes Neural Procedural Mem-
ory (NPM), a training-free framework that in-
tegrates implicit activation steering into agent
memory, enabling effective intrinsic behav-
ioral modulation.
• This paper introduces a dual-granularity ex-
traction method using both inter-trajectory
and intra-trajectory contrasts, offering a flex-
ible intervention mechanism and mitigating
the reliance on successful demonstrations.
• Extensive experiments demonstrate that acti-
vation steering serves as an effective carrier
for agentic skills, yielding interpretable vec-
tors that correlate with specific task behaviors.

evidence.excerpt:
We introduceNeural Procedural Memory
(NPM), a training-free framework designed to in-
ternalize agentic skills directly into the model's
activation space. The framework shown in Fig-
ure 2 consists of three phases: (1)Contrastive
Experience Construction(§3.1), which isolates
effective reasoning patterns from historical failures;
(2)Steering Vector Extraction(§3.2), which dis-
tills discrete textual contrasts into continuous steer-
ing vectors; and (3)Inference-Time Intervention
(§3.3), where these vectors are dynamically synthe-
sized and injected to modulate the agent's behavior.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Task success and reward metrics are computed directly by the external benchmark environments on held-out test tasks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective environment task outcomes: success rate in ALFWorld and task rewards in WebShop, ScienceWorld, and BabyAI.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Historical contrastive trajectories filtered by environment success/failure and deterministic heuristic rules (redundancy loops and execution errors), from which steering vectors are extracted via PCA.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The experimental outcomes align well with the stated claims, demonstrating that dynamic steering vector intervention improves execution success and reward in multi-step agent environments without expanding context token limits.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is evaluated across four standard agent benchmarks (ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld, and BabyAI) using three models (MiniCPM3-4B, Qwen3-4B, and Qwen3-8B), demonstrating solid gains over no-memory and static steering baselines, parity with explicit textual memory, and additive improvements in hybrid setups. Detailed representational, interpretability, and latency analyses are provided.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Task success and reward metrics are computed directly by the external benchmark environments on held-out test tasks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective environment task outcomes, specifically task completion success rate in ALFWorld and task rewards in WebShop, ScienceWorld, and BabyAI.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Historical contrastive trajectories filtered by environmental success/failure and deterministic heuristic rules (redundancy loops and execution errors) to extract steering vectors via PCA.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge key limitations, including the necessity of white-box access to intermediate model activations, vulnerability to cold-start when positive trajectories are sparse, heuristic dependency for identifying degenerate steps, and static application of the steering vector across all execution steps.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the construction of inter-trajectory pairs and intra-trajectory degenerate step identification, representation extraction at intermediate model layers, dynamic synthesis using dense retrieval, and KL-divergence-bounded activation steering during autoregressive decoding.
primary.quality_rationale: The contribution is substantive and well-scoped, the methodological presentation is complete, and empirical validation across multiple interactive environments confirms the effectiveness and efficiency claims with appropriate baselines and controls.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Neural Procedural Memory (NPM), a training-free framework that represents LLM agent procedural memory via activation steering vectors derived from dual-granularity (inter- and intra-trajectory) historical contrasts rather than explicit text prompting.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The contribution is substantive and well-scoped, the methodological presentation is complete, and empirical validation across multiple interactive environments confirms the effectiveness and efficiency claims with appropriate baselines and controls.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge key limitations, including the necessity of white-box access to intermediate model activations, vulnerability to cold-start when positive trajectories are sparse, heuristic dependency for identifying degenerate steps, and static application of the steering vector across all execution steps.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to agentic-memory research based on screening evidence.
